claims.text: The proposed framework integrates organ-level CT context and radiology reports into a unified representation for laryngopharyngeal T-staging.
claims.poster_quote: We propose an anatomy-aware multimodal framework that integrates organ-level CT context and radiology reports into a unified representation for laryngopharyngeal T-staging.

claims.text: The framework constructs an Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) that captures invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs.
claims.poster_quote: The framework first constructs an Anatomy-Structured Organ Graph (AOG) that captures invasion patterns between primary sites and surrounding organs

claims.text: The framework performs Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) so that each organ node aggregates textual evidence from the radiology report.
claims.poster_quote: then performs Organ-Anchored Cross-Modal Alignment (OCA) so that each organ node aggregates textual evidence from the radiology report

claims.text: The framework refines the graph representation by injecting organ-specific invasion cues extracted from the report via Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG).
claims.poster_quote: and finally refines this graph representation by injecting organ-specific invasion cues extracted from the report via Report-Enhanced Graph-Refinement (REG)

claims.text: The setting uses K = 7 predefined anatomical structures.
The primary sites are defined as P = {supraglottic, glottic, subglottic}.
The potentially invaded organs are defined as T = {esophagus, thyroid gland, trachea, oral cavity}.
claims.poster_quote: potentially invaded organs T = {esophagus, thyroid gland, trachea, oral cavity}

claims.text: The model is trained end-to-end with cross-entropy loss for T-staging classification.
claims.poster_quote: The model is trained end-to-end with cross-entropy loss for T-staging classification.
